counter_evidence:
None of the three stated falsifiers holds. (1) The probe (JSON.parse of app.json, /sentry/i over expo.plugins), run read-only through git show, gives: f94ede2 ABSENT, 60c026d PRESENT, b4f0766 PRESENT, a6f9048 ABSENT, c293916 / b818023 / ded44c8 PRESENT, 6928828 / 99df571 / origin/main (a31924a) ABSENT. (2) `git merge-base --is-ancestor 60c026d origin/main` exits 0. (3) PR #59 merged to main at b4f0766 (2026-06-10 11:50:59 +0500). Build 15 failed on 2026-06-26 (6928828 at 16:31; PR #97 merged at 99df571, 16:44). So the plugin was on main 16 days before the burned build.

What does not survive is the mechanism the claim names: a fixed trap's probe "flipping back" after a "re-introduction".
(a) 60c026d did not re-introduce the plugin. It added it for the first time: the diff adds `"@sentry/react-native"` to plugins, and its parent f94ede2 is ABSENT.
(b) The first fix a6f9048 is a child of 60c026d, committed at 16:04:27, about 4h13m after PR #59 had merged (author date equals committer date, so it was not rebased). `git merge-base --is-ancestor a6f9048 origin/main` exits 1, and only refs/remotes/origin/feat/mobile-outbox-v2 contains it. The fix never reached main; it was stranded on the branch.
(c) First-parent history of app.json on origin/main goes from b4f0766 straight to 99df571, and `git log b4f0766..ded44c8 -- technician-app/app.json` is empty. So every main tip from 2026-06-10 11:50:59 to 2026-06-26 16:44:17 is PRESENT, and main never showed ABSENT after the fix existed. A transition detector at origin/main (ABSENT on an earlier scan, then PRESENT) has nothing to fire on. Only a state rule fires: report any validated fixed-trap probe that returns PRESENT at origin/main.
(d) The ex8 control pair the design cites (60c026d / 6928828) did not exist in the window, because 6928828 is dated 2026-06-26 16:31, after build 15. a6f9048 fails the design's own is-ancestor check for mainline controls. In June the entry could only have been validated with passes_at = f94ede2 (an ancestor, exit 0, which is pre-introduction rather than a fix) or with an overlay fixture.
(e) Proposal D's original wording only reverifies entries that `ks scan` first marked suspect because their footprint changed. That fires only if the trace was stamped on the fixer's branch tree (a6f9048's app.json blob). If the trace was stamped at origin/main, the blob never changed and no reverify happens. The v1 doc text "re-runs every validated declarative probe" avoids this, D's mechanism does not.
(f) Build 15 had a second, independent cause already on main. ded44c8 package.json has expo-asset ~56.0.17, expo-crypto ~56.0.4 and expo-location ~56.0.17, against ~11.0.0 / ~14.0.2 / ~18.0.10 at b4f0766. So a flag would not have saved that build.
narrowed_claim: The scan would have flagged ex8 at every phase close on main between 2026-06-10 16:04 (when the fix a6f9048 existed) and 2026-06-26, before build 15, if all of these hold: (i) its rule is state-based, meaning any validated fixed-trap entry whose probe returns PRESENT at origin/main is reported, not only a transition from a previously observed ABSENT; (ii) it re-runs every validated probe unconditionally rather than only entries made suspect by a footprint change; (iii) the entry was validated in that window with a passes_at that passes the is-ancestor check (f94ede2) or an overlay fixture, because a6f9048 is off-main and 6928828 did not exist yet. Under those conditions every main tip from b4f0766 to ded44c8 returns PRESENT. What actually happened in June was not a regression: the fix was committed after PR #59 merged and never landed on main. It is also wrong that the flag would have prevented the burned build, because build 15 also failed on Dependabot's expo-asset, expo-crypto and expo-location bumps to ~56.x, which reached main on 2026-06-16.
design_consequence: §5.2 should specify the phase-close scan as a state check, not an edge check. For every validated fixed or trap entry, report whenever its probe returns PRESENT at origin/main, with no prior ABSENT required. Two labels should replace the single "possible regression": "fix not on main" when the entry's fix commit fails `merge-base --is-ancestor <fix> origin/main` (this is ex8's real June shape), and "regression" when the fix commit is an ancestor and the probe is PRESENT. The scan should re-run all validated probes, not only entries made suspect by a footprint change; drop D's suspect-only gating, or stamp traces against origin/main and run probes regardless. Recording a fix should also check fix-reached-main: if the fix commit is not an ancestor of origin/main, the entry is "fixed on branch only" and is reported at every phase close until it lands. The K-phase deliverable "the ex8 regression scan fires at 60c026d" should be restated as two tests: the scan fires at each origin/main tip from b4f0766 to ded44c8, and a stranded-fix fixture (a fix commit after the PR merge) produces the "fix not on main" label. The ex8 control pair should stay 60c026d / 6928828 for today's tests. The June counterfactual needs f94ede2 or an overlay as passes_at. Finally, drop or qualify the cost claim that the scan would have saved the burned build, since build 15 also failed on the Dependabot ~56.x native bumps. Avoiding that burn needs a second entry or a native-version probe (dep_version against expo/bundledNativeModules.json).
